event.ione_heart2.1.text: A chart of the coast. Every cove drawn by hand. ...You look tired, [player]. Sit while you look; it isn't going anywhere.
event.ione_heart2.1.why: uneasy: she notices the player before the map; plain human care

event.ione_heart2.4.text: There's a cove at the edge, where the ink gives out. ...Someone stopped drawing there. I'd rather think they ran out of ink.
event.ione_heart2.4.why: frightened: the cozy wish curdles into a guess she won't finish

event.ione_heart2.4.text: There's a cove at the very edge, where the ink gives out. The wood comes right down to the water there. Odd, for a coast.
event.ione_heart2.4.why: hint: a place to go; the wood reaching the sea, noticed, not explained

event.ione_heart5.1.text: Would you walk the beach with me one evening? Sea air is good for a tired face. I'm told the tide doesn't mind either way.
event.ione_heart5.1.why: uneasy: the invitation becomes partly for the player's sake

event.ione_heart5.4.text: Evenings, then. I've circled three low tides. None on a new moon. Everyone's home early then; I've never asked why.
event.ione_heart5.4.why: hint: the new-moon custom, seen from outside by someone who never questioned it

event.reading_night.0.text: Every chair, one lamp, and a pot of tea nobody asked for. I lit the lamp early. This is my calm face. Does it work?
event.reading_night.0.why: uneasy: lamps lit early (ladder) worn as nerves; drops the chair-count markup safely

event.reading_night.4.text: A snowdrop, for the lamp. ...Every chair taken, and nobody wants to walk home yet. Stay, all of you. I'll make more tea.
event.reading_night.4.why: frightened: the room is a refuge; she makes it one without asking why

event.reading_night.4.text: A snowdrop, for the lamp. ...Every chair taken. When you go, go together. The lane's darker than it used to be.
event.reading_night.4.why: hint: a small rule she has started keeping without knowing its reason

event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.text: That's the bell. Let them go. ...They're all drifting toward the wood. Every one. It must be the wind. It must be.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.why: frightened: short repeated fragment; the wish she meant for the sea is taken

event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.text: That's the bell. Together now, and slowly. Let them go. ...Mine is drifting toward the wood. I'd meant it for the sea.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.why: uneasy: the same image as cozy, turned inland

event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.text: That's the bell. Let them go. ...Tilda counted the lanterns twice before the bell. She never counts anything twice.
event.festival_winter_lanterns.3.why: hint: a Keeper's too-exact care, noticed by someone who only finds it odd

dlg.ione.shelf.0.text: At the back of the library stands a tall shelf. Every book has a slip tucked inside. No names. Its window faces the wood.
dlg.ione.shelf.0.why: uneasy narration: one placed detail, nothing stated

dlg.ione.shelf.1.text: Books set aside for people who never came. The newest has waited since last fall. It was for Edmund. What would you do?
dlg.ione.shelf.1.why: clue: Edmund's book, set aside the fall he died; the player is the one who can take it

dlg.ione.shelf.r1.text: Aloud? Nobody has ever read these to anyone. Go slowly. ...Your hands are shaking. I'll hold the page steady.
dlg.ione.shelf.r1.why: frightened: she notices the player's hands and stays practical

event.ione_heart8.after.text: {if choice:shelf.take}The first set-aside book to leave the shelf. It's in the ledger. Take it somewhere bright, and tell me once they've read it.{else}{if choice:shelf.read}You read one aloud. The shelf went so quiet. The whole street went... quiet. Read me another, please.{else}I won't move your note. I won't read it. ...Stay a little, though. The shelf feels less alone with you here.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_heart8.after.why: frightened: each branch keeps its meaning; the listening shelf becomes a hush she wants filled

event.ione_heart8.after.text: {if choice:shelf.take}The first set-aside book ever to leave the shelf. It's in the ledger. Tell me who it went to, once they've read it.{else}{if choice:shelf.read}You read one aloud. The shelf has never been so quiet. I'll turn the lamp up, I think.{else}I won't move your note. I won't even read it. ...I'll keep the shelf where I can see it.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_heart8.after.why: uneasy: the same three outcomes, a small reach for light in two of them

event.ione_birthday.after.text: {if choice:bday.ione.wish}Noon came and went, and I never opened the new book. For an hour everything felt ordinary. I needed that.{else}{if choice:bday.ione.read}Someone read to me on my birthday. It's in the ledger, under returned with interest. You read the dark parts gently.{else}The bookmark's holding a very good place. I'd been using a tea label. Things want holding lately.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_birthday.after.why: uneasy: the birthday as a small refuge; branches keep their gifts

event.ione_partners.after.text: {if choice:courtship.ione.letter}The letter's in my favorite book now, marking the best page. Both are yours, eventually.{else}{if choice:courtship.ione.read}Your voice, my library. I've marked the spot where you stood. Nobody else may stand there. Hazel may.{else}The shore was bright. I forgot the book entirely. ...Hazel says not the sea in winter. I'd still like to see it. With you.{/if}{/if}
event.ione_partners.after.why: hint: only the shore branch changes; echoes Hazel's winter-sea warning from the birthday

event.ione_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. The fuss is a new book I don't open until noon. Come in. You look as if you need a fuss too.
event.ione_birthday.intro.why: uneasy: the birthday turns toward the player's tiredness

dlg.ione.birthday.0.text: The new book can wait. Hazel says I mustn't walk to the sea alone this winter. She won't say why. What shall we do?
dlg.ione.birthday.0.why: hint: Hazel's warning reaches the player secondhand; Ione's winter sea is quietly fenced

dlg.ione.birthday.r1.text: The first page, aloud. Nobody's read to me since I was small. ...Read slowly. You keep glancing at the window.
dlg.ione.birthday.r1.why: frightened: closing her eyes would be wrong now; she watches the player instead

event.ione_courtship.intro.text: I've read hundreds of love stories, and none told me how to ask. Things feel uncertain lately, so plainly: would you court me?
event.ione_courtship.intro.why: uneasy: the season's strangeness makes her braver, not darker

dlg.ione.courtship.0.text: What do you say? Take your time. ...You look as if you haven't slept. Sit first. I'll pretend to shelve something.
dlg.ione.courtship.0.why: frightened: the question waits on the player's wellbeing

event.ione_courtship2.intro.text: You asked me to wait. The question sat by the desk bell all through a long, strange season. It held up. Would you court me?
event.ione_courtship2.intro.why: uneasy: names the season's strangeness only as weather of the heart

dlg.ione.partners.0.text: I've set the rest of the day aside for you. You look tired. How shall we spend it, gently?
dlg.ione.partners.0.why: uneasy: one word of care added

dlg.ione.partners.r2.text: The shore, with you. Home before the lamps, though. Everyone is, lately, and nobody tells me why.
dlg.ione.partners.r2.why: clue-tier noticing: the village's hours, from someone left out of them

event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l2.text: You found it. Edmund's copy, margins and all. The library's quiet is yours. I only dust it.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l2.why: clue: points at the almanac with Edmund's margins without repeating the thread line

event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l4.text: Agreed. Back to the tea. Someone ought to light the lamps. It's darker than it should be.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l4.why: uneasy: lamps lit early, as a small complaint

event.overheard_hazel_ione_2.l3.text: I don't much like endings lately either. But seven years on the last chapter?
event.overheard_hazel_ione_2.l3.why: uneasy: keeps the question Hazel answers; one shadowed clause

event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l3.text: You didn't say a word. I heard it anyway. The window's warm after lunch. It faces away from the wood.
event.overheard_hazel_ione_3.l3.why: uneasy: she chose the window on purpose and does not say why

event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l2.text: Dr. Penn. Your clinic was dark at supper and lit at midnight. A new moon, too. I noticed.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l2.why: hint: the leader's night hours, seen by an unaware neighbor; Penn's reply still fits

event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l4.text: Then we'll both go home on time. Before dark, anyway. Everyone seems to, lately.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_1.l4.why: uneasy: the village's early hours noticed

event.overheard_odalys_ione_2.l4.text: Done. The first chapter is two pages. Sleep well, Dr. Penn. You look as if you haven't.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_2.l4.why: uneasy: the Keeper's tiredness seen with plain kindness

event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l2.text: It's the calm kind. Even the stove stopped ticking. Everything's been very quiet lately. Even the birds.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l2.why: uneasy: birds quieter (ladder) slipped into a tea remark

event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l4.text: Always. Here. It's gone a little cold. That's the slow... the slow part working.
event.overheard_odalys_ione_3.l4.why: frightened: a short stammer, the only distortion she gets

adds.text: The almanac was Edmund's. His margins run all year, then stop in the fall. Like this ink.
adds.why: clue: ties the chart to Edmund's stopped margins; a thing to ask Hazel about

adds.text: Actually, it can wait a moment. Sit down first. You look as if you haven't slept.
adds.why: frightened: fills the silence left by cutting the lost-slip joke

cuts.why: the flustered lost-slip joke reads wrong when the player is frightened; the add replaces it with care

notes: Ione is unaware: no ritual vocabulary at any level, no revelation-tier lines; her clues are only things she noticed (Edmund's margins, the set-aside book, new-moon hours, Tilda's counting, Penn's lamp).

dlg.ione.shelf.1 clue invents one small fact: a book set aside for Edmund that waited since last fall. Consistent with the bible (a book set aside for every visitor) and with Edmund dying last fall; flag if Edmund was never a library visitor.
dlg.ione.birthday.0 hint has Hazel warning Ione off the winter sea; Hazel's writer should know so her lines can echo or not contradict it.
